<!-- FORGE:INVESTIGATOR -->
## Investigation Report

### Verdict / Confidence / Severity / Task Type

| Verdict | Confidence | Severity | Task Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| Confirmed | High | Medium | Focused workflow correctness fix with regression coverage |

### What Was Claimed

A successful merge can leave the issue projected with `workflow:awaiting-merge` when post-merge work fails before the merged projection is established. The source finding identifies PR #117 and `src/workflows/work-on.ts` as the affected implementation.

### What We Found

The current integration tree contains two merge execution paths:

- The parent-owned `#runParentNode` path calls `mergePullRequest`, records the merge effect, then projects `workflow:merged`, and only afterward posts review-completion artifacts.
- The legacy/direct `#finalize` path calls `mergePullRequest`, records the merge effect and `merge` phase completion, then projects `workflow:merged`, and only afterward posts review-completion artifacts, closes the issue, and performs cleanup.

This is earlier than the original cited ordering, but the race is not fully closed. In both paths, fallible durable journal writes occur after the merge API succeeds and before the merged projection. In addition, `#projectWorkflowStage` retries projection but ultimately warns and returns, so a projection failure is not a durable terminal guarantee. Any exception between the successful merge and a successful merged projection can leave the previously projected `workflow:awaiting-merge` label in place until a later reconciliation. The attach-time reconciliation can repair some states, but same-session completion failure is still exposed and the projection is not tied to the successful merge at the earliest safe point.

No assigned-worktree diff exists. Existing tests cover label mapping, state transitions, and generic projection idempotency, but do not exercise the successful-merge ordering or a failure window around post-merge work.

### Root Cause

The successful merge side effect and the merged issue projection are modeled as separate best-effort operations with fallible journal/artifact work between them. The workflow can continue into post-merge operations without a focused invariant that `workflow:merged` is attempted immediately after a successful merge and before any later operation that may throw.

### Affected Files

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `src/workflows/work-on.ts` | Merge execution, projection ordering, and recovery paths |
| `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` | Focused regression coverage for merge projection ordering |

### Evidence

- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` parent path: `mergePullRequest` is followed by `effect.recorded`, then `#projectWorkflowStage(link, "merged", ...)`, then `postReviewCompletionArtifacts`.
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` direct path: merge result is followed by `appendEffect`, `appendPhase("merge", "complete", ...)`, then `#projectWorkflowStage(link, "merged", ...)`, then review artifacts, close, and cleanup.
- `#projectWorkflowStage` retries three times but catches projection failures and emits only a warning, so callers cannot distinguish a successful merged projection from an exhausted retry.
- `#reconcileWorkflowProjection` repairs completed merged state on attach, but the cited failure mode can occur before the run reaches terminal completion and no focused regression protects the ordering.
- `WORKFLOW_LABEL_BY_STAGE.merged` is the canonical `workflow:merged` projection and `awaitingMerge` is the prior `workflow:awaiting-merge` projection.

### History Findings

The issue body records the originating review finding as `workflow-correctness-001` from PR #117, source issue #92, at reviewed head `fbdfb397b88b22a8816e59e1d8fab53013f1f309`. The current frozen base already moved the projection ahead of later review artifacts, indicating partial remediation, but retained the vulnerable post-merge journal window and lacks focused regression coverage. No other related issue is required to define this bounded fix.

### Recommendation

Centralize the successful-merge projection boundary and invoke it immediately after `mergePullRequest` returns, before merge journaling or any post-merge artifacts, close, cleanup, or terminal work. Keep the existing retry/reconciliation behavior and invoke the same boundary from both merge paths and terminal recovery where applicable. Add a deterministic source-level or focused workflow regression that fails if any fallible post-merge operation is ordered before the merged projection boundary.

### Related Issues

- #119 — current remediation issue.
- #92 — source issue recorded by the originating review finding.
- PR #117 — source pull request recorded by the finding.

### Decomposition Assessment

- **Required**: No.
- **Reason**: One workflow invariant, one production file, and one focused test file; no independent product, API, or authority decisions.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] A successful merge attempts the canonical `workflow:merged` projection before any subsequent merge journal, artifact, issue-close, cleanup, or terminal operation that can fail.
- [ ] Both parent-node and direct finalization merge paths preserve the invariant without changing merge authority, branch policy, or external side-effect scope.
- [ ] Recovery remains able to re-project `workflow:merged` from durable merge evidence.
- [ ] Focused regression coverage detects a reintroduction of the ordering bug.
- [ ] The configured `check` command passes.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

## Builder Contract

### Objective

Close the successful-merge projection window for issue #119 by attempting the canonical `workflow:merged` label immediately after the merge API returns, before any subsequent merge journaling or post-merge work can fail.

### Allowed Paths

- `src/workflows/work-on.ts`
- `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts`

### Forbidden Changes

- No changes to merge authority, lease validation, branch policy, GitHub API adapters, labels outside the canonical workflow label, or issue/PR scope.
- No changes to `.forge/config.json`, package metadata, CI, schemas, or unrelated workflow phases.
- No new credentials, bypasses, retries outside the existing projection/reconciliation policy, or production-branch behavior.
- No deletion or weakening of existing review, verification, audit, or cleanup gates.

### Invariants

- `mergePullRequest` remains guarded by the existing reviewed-head, base, lease, integration-branch, auto-merge, and clean-diff checks.
- The canonical `WORKFLOW_LABEL_BY_STAGE.merged` value remains the only merged projection.
- Existing projection retries and attach-time reconciliation remain intact.
- Direct and parent-owned merge paths must share the same ordering guarantee.
- The actual merge, durable journal evidence, review artifacts, close, cleanup, and terminal state behavior remain otherwise unchanged.

### Deliverables

- Move the merged projection boundary to immediately follow a successful merge result in both merge execution paths.
- Add focused regression coverage that detects durable bookkeeping or post-merge work preceding the merged projection boundary.

### Acceptance Mapping

| Check | Implementation |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | Both successful merge paths call the canonical merged projection before later journal/artifact/close/cleanup operations. |
| AC-2 | Existing merge authority and recovery logic remain unchanged except for projection ordering. |
| AC-3 | `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` asserts the ordering invariant for the source implementation. |
| AC-4 | Existing `workflowStageForNodeTransition` and reconciliation behavior remain covered by the current test suite. |
| AC-5 | The named `check` verification command passes. |

### Out of Scope

- Reworking GitHub projection retry semantics or adding a new durable projection receipt.
- Refactoring the two existing workflow controllers into a shared abstraction.
- Changes to post-merge institutional-memory artifacts, issue closure, cleanup, or integration orchestration.

## Implementation Context

### History

The originating finding is `workflow-correctness-001` from PR #117, tracked by issue #119 and linked to source issue #92. The frozen base already projects `workflow:merged` before later review artifacts, but still places fallible merge bookkeeping before that projection and has no focused ordering regression.

### Callers And Data Flow

`#runParentNode` handles parent-owned merge nodes during orchestration; `#finalize` handles direct/legacy completion. Both receive a successful `mergePullRequest` result, then perform journal writes, artifact publication, issue closure, cleanup, and terminal transitions. `#projectWorkflowStage` maps `merged` to `workflow:merged`, retries projection, and warns after exhausted attempts. `#reconcileWorkflowProjection` remains the restart repair path for durable merged state.

### CI Surface

The tracked command is `check` (`npm run check`), which runs TypeScript typechecking and the complete `test/**/*.test.ts` suite. GitHub CI remains parent-owned after PR preparation.

### Prior Findings

The accepted finding is a medium-severity correctness issue: a durable successful merge can remain projected as `workflow:awaiting-merge` if an operation between the merge API and merged label projection throws. The current code has partial ordering remediation but needs the earliest safe projection boundary and regression coverage.

### Hazards

- Do not move projection before merge API success or alter merge authority.
- Do not remove the review-label fallback on merge API failure.
- Preserve the already-merged/idempotent path and terminal recovery behavior.
- Keep the regression deterministic and independent of GitHub credentials or production issue data.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->
<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT -->
## Implementation Plan

1. In the parent-owned merge branch, invoke `#projectWorkflowStage(link, "merged", ...)` immediately after `mergePullRequest` returns; leave the existing merge effect, node completion, and post-review artifact sequence unchanged after that boundary.
2. In the direct/legacy finalization branch, invoke the same merged projection immediately after the successful/new-or-already-merged result is established; remove the later duplicate invocation so journal phase completion and post-merge operations cannot precede it.
3. Add a focused test in `test/workflows/work-on.test.ts` that reads the implementation and asserts, for both merge paths, that the successful merge result precedes the merged projection and that the projection precedes durable merge bookkeeping and post-merge artifact work.
4. Run the configured `check` command through `forge_verify`, inspect the resulting diff, and commit only the two contracted files.

### Acceptance Checks

- [ ] Parent-owned merge projection is ordered immediately after successful merge result.
- [ ] Direct/legacy merge projection is ordered immediately after successful merge result.
- [ ] Regression coverage fails on a later projection ordering.
- [ ] Existing behavior and safety gates remain unchanged.
- [ ] `check` passes.
